description:
Hi! I'm an aspiring astrobiologist and a BSc Microbiology student from India, passionate about space exploration, astrobiology, space biology, molecular microbiology, and the future of human exploration on the Moon and Mars.

I enjoy researching innovative ideas, scientific problem-solving, and developing space-related projects. I'm looking for passionate teammates with skills in programming, AI/ML, astronomy, engineering, 3D modelling, data science, and scientific research.
summary: BIOCOSMOSZ is an interactive web platform that helps researchers and students find and understand Earth analog sites for Mars and the Moon. It goes beyond visual similarity. Each site is rated separately on eight dimensions: geology, terrain, temperature, water and ice, dust and erosion, biology, caves and subsurface, and operations. Users set their own priorities and see what matches and what does not. It combines a 3D globe and map of analog sites, an extremophile database, a Mars/Moon/Earth environment comparison, a mission dashboard and real NASA POWER climate data retrieved live. It also highlights lesser-known analogs such as lava tubes, impact craters and Serpentinising rocks. Every score is labelled as a project heuristic, and modelled or sample data is never presented as live NASA data.
details:
What it does: BIOCOSMOSZ is a web application with an interactive 3D globe and map of Earth analog sites, an extremophile database, a Mars/Earth/Moon environment comparison, a mission dashboard linking to official NASA pages, a live NASA POWER data viewer, and an Analog Discovery tool.

How it works: Analog Discovery rates 12 candidate Earth sites for a Mars or Moon target on eight dimensions. Users set the weight of each dimension through goal presets (biosignatures, water/ISRU, human operations, robotic mobility, subsurface shelter) or sliders. The temperature dimension is computed from NASA POWER climatology retrieved live for each site's coordinates (annual mean air temperature T2M compared with Mars's roughly -63 C; for the Moon, the T2M_MAX minus T2M_MIN range is used as a weak proxy). If NASA POWER is unreachable, the page clearly labels the score as a project heuristic. All other ratings are project judgements based on qualitative descriptions of each site, and the site says so. Each result explains why the site was chosen, its differences from the target, the key process involved (for example serpentinisation or wind erosion) and experiments that could be run there.

Benefits: It shows that an analog can be strong in one dimension and weak in another, helps match sites to research goals, and highlights lesser-studied sites and sub-areas such as a single crater or lava tube.

Limits: Scores are a project-created heuristic, not an official NASA assessment or validated prediction. Earth cannot reproduce reduced gravity, the lunar vacuum, the thin Martian atmosphere or their radiation environments, and the site states this.

Goal: A transparent starting point for choosing analog sites, extendable with more NASA Earth-observation datasets such as elevation, ice and aerosols.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, Leaflet, Chart.js, NASA POWER API.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) AP
Hassler et al. 2014, Science (Mars surface radiation, Curiosity RAD)
Zhang et al. 2020, Science Advances (Moon surface radiation, Chang’e-4)
